# Content formats and scoring

## Searchable formats

- **Use-case pages**: [persona] + [use case], for example "inventory tracking for small bakeries". Good for specific, lower-competition searches.
- **Hub and spoke**: one comprehensive hub page per major topic, with linked spoke articles for subtopics. Build the hub first. Most content can simply live in the blog with good internal links; dedicated hub URLs are only worth it for deep topics.
- **Templates and checklists**: useful on their own and show how the product helps.
- **Glossary and definition pages**: answer "what is" questions clearly.
- **How-to tutorials**: step-by-step answers to implementation questions.

## Shareable formats

- **Thought leadership**: name a problem everyone feels, or challenge common advice with evidence.
- **Data pieces**: anonymized product data, public data analysis or original research.
- **Statistics roundups**: a maintained, cited page of statistics for the category. Writers link to whatever is easiest to cite, so these tend to earn links well.
- **Expert roundups**: many experts answer one specific question.
- **Case studies**: challenge, solution, results, lessons. Only with the customer's permission.
- **Behind the scenes**: honest accounts of how the company works or decided something.

## Scoring template

Score 1-10 per factor, multiply by the weight, add up.

| Idea | Customer impact (40%) | Content-market fit (30%) | Search potential (20%) | Resources, higher = easier (10%) | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Example A | 8 | 9 | 7 | 6 | 7.9 |
| Example B | 6 | 7 | 9 | 8 | 7.1 |

- Customer impact: how often the topic came up, how many customers face it, how painful it is.
- Content-market fit: alignment with what the company sells, unique insight available, customer stories available.
- Search potential: demand, competition, related long-tail topics, trend direction.
- Resources: expertise in-house, research and assets needed.

## Per-format production habits

- Blog post: write about 10 title options before drafting; plan several editing passes (structure, clarity, evidence, line edit, title and search).
- Long guide: table of contents, links to related articles; hub before spokes.
- Video: script the hook first and show the payoff early; plan short clips at creation time.
- Podcast or interview: plan the transcript, quotes, short clips and a written recap before recording.
- Email: one idea per send; write several subject lines and pick one.

## Distribution failure modes

- Posting everywhere with no flagship piece and no reuse plan.
- Depending on one rented platform whose reach can drop overnight.
- Spending most effort on channels the company does not control while neglecting its email list and website.
